title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 112
paragraphs: Having passed through the country just described, Xerxes next went by the strongholds of the Pierians, one of which is called Phagres and the other Pergamos. This way he made his march, passing close under the walls of these places and keeping Mount Pangaeum on his right, which is both great and lofty and has mines of gold and silver held by the Pierians and the Odomantians, and especially by the Satrae.
